title: heap-use-after-free in sqlite3BtreeRollback
live_proof: inspection with line numbers in the 3.22.0 tree, confirmed by a host ASan run 2026-10-15: sqlite3_backup caches raw Btree* at backup.c:23 and :29, resolved by findBtree at :82, and detachFunc closes that Btree at attach.c:292 (sqlite3BtreeClose) while the backup still holds the pointer. detachFunc's own guard does not cover it: sqlite3BtreeIsInBackup reads Btree.nBackup, and backup.c:205 increments it on the SOURCE only. Host ASan reports heap-use-after-free in sqlite3BtreeRollback <- sqlite3_backup_finish, freed by sqlite3BtreeClose <- detachFunc, allocated by sqlite3BtreeOpen <- attachFunc. Fixed upstream in 3.53.3 by storing db indices and re-deriving the Btree at each use
object: the Btree of the destination database the backup caches, allocated by attachFunc
lifetime_ender: DETACH of the destination database on the destination connection closes that Btree (detachFunc -> sqlite3BtreeClose)
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator: the public backup API driven against a connection that DETACHes the destination database mid-backup. The backup is stepped to SQLITE_DONE first because detachFunc also refuses a database in a read transaction, and that commit (backup.c:567) ends the destination's; p->bDestLocked stays 1, so no later step reopens one
